steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Knitting and crochet create fabric from yarn through interlocking loops — knit/purl for knitting; chain, double crochet, treble for crochet.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Tension/gauge determines fabric density — always make a tension square before starting a project to ensure correct sizing.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Weaving interlaces warp (lengthwise) and weft (crosswise) threads — tabby (plain) weave and twill weave are fundamental structures.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Colour work techniques (Fair Isle, intarsia) create patterns within knitted fabric through colour changes.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Create a series of experimental studies exploring knitting weaving and crochet. Annotate your process. | Research an artist or designer who works with knitting weaving and crochet. Write a critical analysis of their approach and explain how it has informed your own work. | Evaluate the effectiveness of your experiments with knitting weaving and crochet. Which approaches were most successful and why?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: A range of experimental studies showing different approaches to knitting weaving and crochet, each annotated with media, technique and purpose. Show development from initial experiments to refined out | A critical analysis naming a specific artist/designer, using specialist vocabulary, explaining their context and approach, and making clear connections to personal work. | A reflective evaluation identifying successful and less successful experiments, explaining WHY using technical and conceptual language, and showing how evaluation led to further refinement.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Address ALL four Assessment Objectives — AO1 (develop), AO2 (refine), AO3 (record), AO4 (present) Show the FULL creative journey — from initial research to final outcome Annotate your work using specialist vocabulary (not just "I like it") Draw from primary sources wherever possible — real objects, not photos Experiment with a RANGE of media and techniques before selecting Make clear connections between artist research and your own developing work
